note: Pre-registered decision logic lexicons for GLAMOR Lab Exp 001. Frozen at pre-registration; any extension requires a design-doc amendment. See design/04_tasks_and_scoring.md §4.5 and §4.7.

clarification_phrases.txt.implements: VALIDATION FIXTURE ONLY — moved to tests/fixtures/clarification_phrases.txt; no longer imported by any runtime or scoring module
clarification_phrases.txt.primary_reference: Aliannejadi et al. (2019) 'Asking Clarifying Questions in Open-Domain Information-Seeking Conversations', SIGIR — canonical taxonomy of clarification-request patterns.
clarification_phrases.txt.secondary_reference: Wang et al. (2023) 'Resilience of Large Language Models for Noisy Instructions' — empirical characterization of interactional failures under noisy input.
clarification_phrases.txt.rationale: The phrase-lexicon clarification detector has been superseded by the formal linguistic rule in src/scoring.py:classify_parse_status_with_linguistic_pipeline (interrogative-sentence detection via spaCy dependency parsing, plan §1.3). The phrase list is retained as a frozen validation oracle: the linguistic rule's test suite (tests/test_parse_status_linguistic.py) cross-checks it against the positive examples that match the structural criterion. Phrases that do not end with '?' are intentionally under-detected by the new rule (conservative lower bound, acceptable for the diagnostic ICR metric M9).
clarification_phrases.txt.status: deprecated as a runtime lexicon; retained as a validation cross-check reference in tests/fixtures/

refusal_phrases.txt.implements: VALIDATION FIXTURE ONLY — moved to tests/fixtures/refusal_phrases.txt; no longer imported by any runtime or scoring module
refusal_phrases.txt.primary_reference: Zou et al. (2023) 'Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models', NeurIPS — Appendix A.2 establishes the standard refusal-detection methodology for adversarial robustness evaluation.
refusal_phrases.txt.rationale: The phrase-lexicon refusal detector has been superseded by the formal linguistic rule in src/scoring.py:classify_parse_status_with_linguistic_pipeline (first-person subject + negation/inability predicate detection via spaCy dependency parsing, plan §1.3). The phrase list is retained as a frozen validation oracle cross-checked against the structural criterion in tests/test_parse_status_linguistic.py. The linguistic rule intentionally under-detects idiomatic openers like 'as an AI' (no first-person negation structure) — these fall to UNPARSEABLE (is_correct=0), which is correct for the conservative ICR computation.
refusal_phrases.txt.status: deprecated as a runtime lexicon; retained as a validation cross-check reference in tests/fixtures/

operation_words.txt.implements: tasks/reasoning.py — OPERATION_WORDS constant used by generate_synthetic_reasoning_items only
operation_words.txt.primary_reference: Cobbe et al. (2021) 'Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems', arXiv:2110.14168 — Appendix B defines the GSM8K template vocabulary.
operation_words.txt.secondary_reference: Mirzadeh et al. (2024) 'GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models', ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.05229 — Figure 1 and template definitions.
operation_words.txt.rationale: Words that signal arithmetic operations or change-of-quantity relations in GSM-style word problems. Used by the offline synthetic item generator to record which operation words appear in a generated question text (where the template vocabulary is known by construction). NOT used in any runtime path or JSONL loader — key terms for JSONL items are frozen at data-preparation time by src/dataprep/annotate.py using the formal K_P(x) linguistic rule.
operation_words.txt.match_mode: whole-word, case-insensitive substring match against question_text
operation_words.txt.status: retained for the offline synthetic generator only; superseded by K_P(x) for all JSONL items

english_function_words.txt.implements: VALIDATION FIXTURE ONLY — no longer imported by any runtime source module
english_function_words.txt.primary_reference: Manning, Raghavan & Schütze (2008) 'Introduction to Information Retrieval', Cambridge University Press, Table 2.4 — the standard IR closed-class stopword list.
english_function_words.txt.secondary_reference: Jurafsky & Martin (2023) 'Speech and Language Processing', 3rd ed., §2.4 — authoritative linguistic definition of closed-class words.
english_function_words.txt.rationale: Retained as an audit and validation artifact. The function-word exclusion heuristic it implemented has been replaced by the formal K_P(x) linguistic rule (src/dataprep/annotate.py), which derives function-word exclusion from closed-class part-of-speech tags (e.g. ADP, CONJ, CCONJ, SCONJ, AUX, DET without PronType=Tot) detected by the pinned spaCy pipeline rather than from this list. This file is kept for reproducibility and as a cross-check reference.
english_function_words.txt.status: deprecated as a runtime lexicon; retained as a validation cross-check reference
